title: Pidilite Industries Ltd - 500331 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Pidilite Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 15.3% to INR 3,272 crore on 15.3% UVG, with EBITDA margin up 280 bps to 23.4%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: standalone revenue grew 15.3% on underlying volume growth (UVG) of 15.3%, with Consumer & Bazaar at 15.4% and B2B at 14.8%. Gross margin improved about 100 bps YoY and costs below gross margin grew only 9.2%, lifting EBITDA 31.1% and margin to 23.4%. PAT grew slower than EBITDA because of timing of subsidiary dividends and mark-to-market losses on treasury income. Management flagged a sharp raw material inflation shock (40-50% on weighted basket, VAM up sharply from West Asia conflict), with two price hikes taken in April and May, and declined to guide FY27 UVG.

segments.name: Consumer & Bazaar
segments.commentary: UVG of 15.4% in Q4 FY26; growth brands Roff and Dr. Fixit at the higher end of guidance, and Fevicol grew double digits.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: UVG of 14.8% in Q4 FY26; exports disrupted in March 2026 due to West Asia conflict, after strong performance through February.

segments.name: Domestic subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 5.3% in Q4 FY26; Nina waterproofing declined about 16% on site-work restrictions (pollution curbs), while the rest, mainly Consumer & Bazaar, grew very strongly.

segments.name: Paints (rural/small towns)
segments.commentary: Management said Rurban India (rural and very small towns) is growing well in the five Southern states plus West Bengal and Bihar; small-town expansion model still a work in progress.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin corridor of 20-24% reaffirmed for the year; management said FY26 was at the higher end with benign inputs and FY27 will be different given inflation.
No explicit UVG guidance for FY27; management aims for about 100 bps UVG expansion over FY26 but said it is too early to guess for this year.
Management expects demand compression in FY27 due to inflation; full-year volume not expected to match Q4 run-rate, though Q1 momentum may sustain.
Price increases: about 4-5% in April and 7-8% in early May at blended company level; further pricing will depend on raw material trajectory, and pass-back is possible if inputs cool.
Capex guided at 3-5% of revenue; FY26 capex about INR 570 crore vs INR 430 crore in FY25; large West India plant for premium white glue and Fevicol to be commissioned in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR 570 crore vs INR 430 crore in FY25, within a 3-5% of revenue band.
Capex split into three buckets: growth capex, automation/consolidation/renovation of core categories (premium white glue), and newer categories.
Large plant in West India for premium white glue and Fevicol to be commissioned in Q1 FY27.
Management said it holds high VAM inventory cover (above normal) to protect Q1 FY27 supply.
Supply security said to be largely secured for Q1 FY27 across raw materials; alternative sourcing (including China) being explored for VAM after Saudi supplier disruption.
demand_pricing: Raw material basket inflation of 40-50% at current replacement prices (weighted average, company-wide); some raw materials coming off peak as of mid-May.
VAM around $1,800/tonne per management; Q4 FY26 VAM averaged about $840/tonne, in line with Q3. VAM was under 10% of raw material consumption in FY25-26; expected to be higher this year.
Price increases: about 4-5% in April and 7-8% in early May at blended company level; Fevicol division about 12-15% cumulative (5% April, 7-9% May).
Management said competitors also took similar price increases, some already in March. Strategy is calibrated pass-through, prioritising volume growth over margin.
Management said urban demand buoyancy seen across Q4 and February was very strong; Nina and tile-related Roff demand affected by gas shortages in Morbi, but tile stock in the channel is high.

Management said share gains in tile adhesives and growth categories; unorganised players likely struggling with supply volatility. Management said it has no direct benefit from GST cuts, attributing discretionary demand to GST changes and budget tax relief.

qa_highlights.question: Why transfer BuildNext to JSW One in exchange for shares, and is this financial or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the BuildNext transfer was for strategic synergies, with JSW One a better home for BuildNext; Pidilite will be a small shareholder with insignificant stake. Further synergies, including paints, would be explored over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% volume growth a one-off or due to any Middle East business transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs; buoyancy in urban demand, possibly helped by GST 2.0 and budget relief, and intensified demand generation. Q4 Fevicol grew double digits; growth brands at higher end of band.

qa_highlights.question: What is the extent of supply disruption and the price hikes taken in response to VAM inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply security largely secured for the quarter; raw material inflation 40-50%; price hikes of about 4-5% in April and 7-8% in May, blended. Management said a significant part of rupee cost increase has been factored in and some reversal has begun as oil fell from $110 to below $100.

qa_highlights.question: How is Roff demand holding up given gas shortages affecting tile production in Morbi?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged gas-powered industries were impacted; said tile channel stock is high, so near-term impact is limited unless a protracted conflict with severe gas shortages occurs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the price elasticity and likely volume backlash from pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formula; said FY27 will see some demand compression from inflation, timing and size unpredictable, and full-year volume growth at the Q4 rate should not be assumed, though Q1 momentum may hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 UVG be higher than FY26 (11-15%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is planning about 100 bps UVG expansion over FY26, but would not guess given the unusual year; intent to reinvest margin headroom behind growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% volume growth driven by trade channel stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no channel loading in March; the company followed its usual practice of going slow in late March and accelerating in April. Management attributed growth to demand buoyancy, growth categories, field marketing and some share gain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely EBITDA margin for FY27 at crude of $85-90?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin depends on overall raw material inflation, not just crude; reaffirmed 20-24% corridor and said it stays committed, with FY26 at upper end and FY27 likely different.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (40-50% basket; VAM) and pace of pass-through; potential demand compression as price increases feed through in FY27.
West Asia conflict: duration affects supply security, export volumes (March disruption), and VAM sourcing from Saudi Arabia (now shifting to other sources).
Gas supply shortages affecting gas-powered industries including Morbi tile production, with possible knock-on effect on Roff demand if conflict is protracted.
Q1 FY27 volume momentum and whether price-led growth affects UVG; management declined to guide FY27 UVG.
Nina waterproofing declined about 16% in Q4 FY26 due to site restrictions; quarterly volatility remains.
Treasury income volatility from rising bond yields; subsidiary dividend timing affecting reported PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 volume and demand momentum, but cautious and noncommittal on FY27, repeatedly declining to quantify full-year UVG, pricing elasticity or margin, citing an unusually dynamic cost and geopolitical environment.
